record.title: Peritoneal Effusion in a Dog due toBabesia gibsoniInfection
record.abstract: A five-year-old male Labrador was presented to Teaching Veterinary Clinics of GADVASU with a primary complaint of distended abdomen, fever, and anorexia. The dog was found to be dull with elevated rectal temperature (104°F), heart rate (148 per minute), and respiration rate (58 per minute). Blood smear examination and PCR assay revealed that dog was positive forBabesia gibsoni. Elevated bilirubin, alanine amino transferase (ALT), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), creatinine, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), total leucocyte count, hypoalbuminaemia, and hypoproteinaemia were haematobiochemical alterations. Radiography and ultrasonography showed ground glass appearance and anechoic area of abdomen, respectively.

screening.rationale: Case of B. gibsoni infection presenting with peritoneal effusion, hypoalbuminaemia and hepatic/renal biochemical changes, an uncommon presentation that bears on vascular permeability and fluid distribution.
